 Fort Madison Fire Department crews will be out monitoring local condition after the two controlled detonations scheduled for Friday at around noon at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown.
 The U.S. Army is conducting the operation to dispose of degraded lead azide under an emergency permit issued by the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency.
 “I’ve heard from residents who want to know what this could mean for Fort Madison,” Fort Madison Fire Chief Chad Hannum said in a press release.
 “Our crews will be out Friday afternoon, and we’ll be following the Army’s updates.
 “If conditions change or there’s guidance our residents need to follow, we’ll share it through the City’s official channels.”
 The Army expects the operation to produce a plume containing lead particles. Its maps show where airborne particles or dust could travel under forecast conditions, and the Army plans to update those maps as weather conditions change.
 The National Weather Service currently forecasts winds from the south, blowing generally northward, in the Burlington area around the time of the operation.
 That forecast may change before Friday.
 The Fort Madison Fire Department says they will monitor local conditions and relay verified information relevant to Fort Madison.
 The Army is conducting air sampling at the plant perimeter and plans to issue an updated estimate of the affected area after the operation.
 Residents can find the latest maps and protective guidance in the U.S. Army public advisory. army.mil
